hunks.baseline: When a battle that has left behind countless dead and rivers of blood finally ends, victory and defeat are decided. Those who survive gather in one place and prepare for the battle of tomorrow.
hunks.sol: When a battle that has left countless deaths and rivers of blood finally ends, victory and defeat are decided. The survivors gather in one place and prepare for tomorrow’s battle.

hunks.baseline: The first to break the silence was a middle-aged soldier who looked to be in his forties. Wearing a uniform caked in dried blood, he continued in an exhausted voice.
hunks.sol: The first to break the silence was a middle-aged soldier who looked to be in his forties. His uniform caked with dried blood, he continued in a weary voice.

hunks.baseline: “We managed to hold the high ground by the skin of our teeth, but we lost more than three thousand troops in a single day.”
hunks.sol: “We barely managed to hold the high ground, but we lost more than three thousand troops today alone.”

hunks.baseline: Three thousand troops was an enormous loss in itself, but the bigger problem was that more than thirty percent of the dead were Hunters, including the commander and several high-ranking officers.
hunks.sol: Three thousand troops was an enormous loss in itself, but the greater problem was that Hunters accounted for more than thirty percent of the dead, including the commander and several high-ranking officers.

hunks.baseline: Even taking into account the three-to-one difference in troop numbers, the damage was staggering.
hunks.sol: Even considering the threefold disparity in troop strength, the blow was devastating.

hunks.baseline: “Did headquarters send a reply?”
hunks.sol: “Has headquarters sent a reply?”

hunks.baseline: “Of course. They said they’ll send a new commander before dawn after holding an internal meeting.”
hunks.sol: “Yes. They said they’ll hold an internal meeting and dispatch a new commander before dawn.”

hunks.baseline: “That’s a relief, at least. Then, do you happen to know who the new commander will be…?”
hunks.sol: “That’s a relief, at least. Then do you happen to know who the new commander will be…?”

hunks.baseline: As people exchanged words in the somber atmosphere, someone suddenly spoke up.
hunks.sol: As they spoke amid the somber atmosphere, someone abruptly cut in.

hunks.baseline: “A relief? Do you all really think that?”
hunks.sol: “A relief? Do you all really think so?”

hunks.baseline: Words spoken by someone who had remained silent carried weight. Even more so when that person was a living hero of the Great Cataclysm and an S-rank Hunter.
hunks.sol: The words of someone who had remained silent carried weight. Even more so when that person was a living hero of the Great Cataclysm and an S-rank Hunter.

hunks.baseline: “Half the command staff, including the commander, were torn to pieces by the flying monsters. The troops under them panicked, which only made the casualties worse. Can you really call a situation like this a relief?”
hunks.sol: “Half the command staff, including the commander, were torn apart by flying monsters. The troops under them panicked, driving the casualties even higher. Can you really call any part of that a relief?”

hunks.baseline: The people flinched beneath the gaze filled with an irresistible aura.
hunks.sol: Everyone flinched beneath the irresistible force of her gaze.

hunks.baseline: “You’re trying to make excuses, so I suppose you do know. But…”
hunks.sol: “The fact that you’re trying to make excuses means you know I’m right. But…”

hunks.baseline: A chilly voice slipped from between red lips.
hunks.sol: A chilling voice slipped between red lips.

hunks.baseline: Faye Chen’s gaze moved across the room before stopping abruptly on one man.
hunks.sol: Faye Chen’s gaze swept across the room, then stopped abruptly on one man.

hunks.baseline: “Why don’t you have any excuses?”
hunks.sol: “Why aren’t you even trying to make an excuse?”

hunks.baseline: After a brief silence, Wu Heixing swirled the alcohol in his crystal glass.
hunks.sol: After a brief silence, Wu Heixing swirled the liquor in his crystal glass.

hunks.baseline: “Why should I make excuses?”
hunks.sol: “Why should I?”

hunks.baseline: “If you’re asking why, well…”
hunks.sol: “Why? Well…”

hunks.baseline: Faye Chen’s eyes deepened.
hunks.sol: Faye Chen’s eyes darkened.

hunks.baseline: “Maybe it’s because some fucking idiot abandoned the area he was assigned to, allowing the flying monsters waiting for that moment to tear the command headquarters apart?”
hunks.sol: “Maybe because some fucking idiot abandoned his assigned position, giving the flying monsters waiting for that exact moment the chance to tear command headquarters apart?”

hunks.baseline: “I did it to help the front line.”
hunks.sol: “…I went to support the front line.”

hunks.baseline: Wu Heixing’s answer was nothing more than a pathetic excuse. When he abandoned the rear, the troops on the front line under Faye Chen’s command had been successfully holding back the endless assault of the monster army.
hunks.sol: Wu Heixing’s answer was nothing more than a pathetic excuse. When he abandoned the rear, the troops under Faye Chen’s command had been holding the front line against the monster army’s endless assault without any trouble.

hunks.baseline: “Oh, right. There was that, too. You went charging deep into enemy territory like an ignorant brat because you wanted to earn some military glory, and the formation collapsed. The kids who chased after you to save your ass—do you even know that their bodies were never found?”
hunks.sol: “Oh, right. There was that, too. You charged deep into enemy territory like some clueless brat because you wanted all the glory, and the formation collapsed. Those kids who went after you to save your ass—did you even know they never found their bodies?”

hunks.baseline: “Life and death are common occurrences on a battlefield.”
hunks.sol: “People live and die on the battlefield all the time.”

hunks.baseline: “Of course. They’re very common.”
hunks.sol: “Of course. It happens all the time.”

hunks.baseline: Faye Chen continued in a low voice.
hunks.sol: Faye Chen continued quietly.

hunks.baseline: “People like you dying without anyone knowing used to be even more common. Come to think of it, the world has gotten pretty nice. If this had been during the Great Cataclysm…”
hunks.sol: “Back then, people like you disappearing without a trace was even more common. Come to think of it, the world has gotten awfully forgiving. If this had been during the Great Cataclysm…”

hunks.baseline: But Faye Chen’s words never reached the end.
hunks.sol: But Faye Chen never got to finish.

hunks.baseline: Crystal shards flew in every direction with a sharp sound.
hunks.sol: A sharp crack rang out as crystal shards flew in every direction.

hunks.baseline: Wu Heixing slowly rose to his feet after smashing his glass.
hunks.sol: Having crushed the glass in his hand, Wu Heixing slowly rose to his feet.

hunks.baseline: “Enough? You’re getting awfully casual with your words.”
hunks.sol: “Enough? You’re getting awfully informal with me.”

hunks.baseline: “There’s a limit to how much I can tolerate, Faye Chen.”
hunks.sol: “There’s a limit to how much I’ll tolerate, Faye Chen.”

hunks.baseline: “Go on. Keep talking. Just remember that as your words get shorter, so does your lifespan.”
hunks.sol: “Go on, then. Keep talking. Just remember—the more casual your tone gets, the shorter your lifespan becomes.”

hunks.baseline: “How dare a Hong Konger who’s practically a traitor—!”
hunks.sol: “How dare some Hong Konger who’s practically a traitor—!”

hunks.baseline: “Ah. If you mean the Hong Konger who cleaned up the front line you shat all over, then I suppose that’s me.”
hunks.sol: “Ah. If you mean the Hong Konger who cleaned up the front line you shat all over, then yes, I suppose that’s me.”

hunks.baseline: The tremendous auras flowing from the two of them spread through the room. Under the overwhelming pressure, the people could barely breathe.
hunks.sol: The tremendous auras pouring from the two of them engulfed the room. The pressure was so overwhelming that the others could barely breathe.

hunks.baseline: The brief standoff between the two S-rank Hunters ended the next moment with a mocking smile appearing at the corner of Faye Chen’s mouth.
hunks.sol: Then, in the next instant, the brief standoff between the two S-rank Hunters ended as a mocking smile touched Faye Chen’s lips.

hunks.baseline: “You’re scared and exhausted, but you still want to earn military glory. That’s why you’re getting more desperate by the day, isn’t it?”
hunks.sol: “You’re scared and exhausted, but you still want the glory. That’s why you’re growing more desperate by the day, isn’t it?”

hunks.baseline: “Kid, that’s what war is like. It always drives people to the edge and tests them. You need a strong mind to endure hell like this. For an immature child like you, who’s always lived however he pleased, it was bound to be difficult.”
hunks.sol: “Kid, that’s what war does. It drives people to the brink and tests them. You need a strong mind to endure a hell like this. Of course it’s hard for a spoiled child like you who’s always done whatever he pleased.”

hunks.baseline: Wu Heixing’s face twisted grotesquely. Every one of Faye Chen’s words had struck him in the heart.
hunks.sol: Wu Heixing’s face twisted grotesquely. Every word out of Faye Chen’s mouth had struck home.

hunks.baseline: “An S-rank Hunter? So what? Mentally, you’re nothing more than a seven-year-old child. Someone like you is worse than useless in a war like this.”
hunks.sol: “An S-rank Hunter? So what? Mentally, you’re nothing but a seven-year-old child. In a war like this, we’d be better off without someone like you.”

hunks.baseline: “Shut your mouth! What the hell do you know…?”
hunks.sol: “Shut up! What the hell do you know…?”

hunks.baseline: “What do I know? Are you saying that to me?”
hunks.sol: “What do I know? You’re asking me that?”

hunks.baseline: At Faye Chen’s derisive snort, Wu Heixing’s face flushed bright red.
hunks.sol: Faye Chen’s derisive snort made Wu Heixing’s face flush bright red.

hunks.baseline: He had been born with power and wealth in both hands, but his opponent was a war hero who had fought her way through the Great Cataclysm firsthand.
hunks.sol: He had been born with wealth and power in both hands, but his opponent was a war hero who had fought her way through the Great Cataclysm.

hunks.baseline: The media had discriminated against Faye Chen because she was from Hong Kong, but when it came to experience, Wu Heixing could not hold a candle to her.
hunks.sol: The media discriminated against Faye Chen for being from Hong Kong, but when it came to experience, she was someone Wu Heixing could never hope to match.

hunks.baseline: Grinding his teeth and refusing to respond, Wu Heixing swept his gaze around the room.
hunks.sol: Wu Heixing clenched his teeth, refusing to respond, and swept his gaze around the room.

hunks.baseline: No one had bothered to say anything aloud, but the looks in their eyes resembled Faye Chen’s.
hunks.sol: No one said anything aloud, but their eyes held the same contempt as Faye Chen’s.

hunks.baseline: *You’ve got to be fucking kidding me…*
hunks.sol: *These fucking bastards…!*

hunks.sol: Even more infuriating was that some of them belonged to the Crown Prince Party and had close ties to Wu Heixing.

hunks.sol: The Crown Prince Party was the largest faction within the Chinese Communist Party. As a blood descendant of one of its most prominent leaders, Wu Heixing felt betrayed to the bone.

hunks.baseline: “I’ll remember what happened today. Every bit of it.”
hunks.sol: “I’ll remember what happened today. Every last bit of it.”

hunks.baseline: Wu Heixing turned away after leaving those words behind, thick fumes of liquor trailing from him.
hunks.sol: Leaving those furious words behind, Wu Heixing turned away.

hunks.baseline: Faye Chen’s low voice flew after him and struck him in the back.
hunks.sol: As he departed reeking of liquor, Faye Chen’s quiet voice flew after him and struck him squarely in the back.

hunks.baseline: “Remember this, too. A child’s little act of bravado ends today. If a situation like today’s happens again… I won’t forgive you next time.”
hunks.sol: “Remember this, too. Today is the last day I’ll tolerate a child’s reckless bravado. If this happens again… I won’t forgive you.”

hunks.baseline: Grind.
hunks.sol: Grit.

hunks.baseline: The first thing Wu Heixing did after returning to his quarters, grinding his teeth, was smash everything within sight.
hunks.sol: Wu Heixing returned to his quarters grinding his teeth. The first thing he did was smash everything in sight.

hunks.baseline: “Fucking Hong Kong bitch! You goddamn traitor bastards!”
hunks.sol: “Fucking Hong Kong bitch! Fucking traitorous bastards!”

hunks.sol: The expensive luxury furnishings he had brought over on his private jet despite the chaos shattered into pieces.

hunks.baseline: After stomping and breaking whatever he could reach while screaming like a madman, Wu Heixing finally lay down on the bed, breathing heavily.
hunks.sol: He spent a long while stomping and smashing everything within reach, screaming like a madman. At last, breathing heavily, Wu Heixing threw himself onto the bed.

hunks.baseline: The anger refused to subside.
hunks.sol: His anger refused to subside.

hunks.baseline: Rather than fading, it only grew hotter the more he thought about it. His heart pounded, and his vision nearly turned white.
hunks.sol: Far from fading, it burned hotter the more he thought about it. His heart pounded so violently that his vision nearly went white.

hunks.baseline: He had been born into the family of one of the most powerful men in China and had risen all the way to this point.
hunks.sol: He had been born into one of the most powerful families in China and risen all the way to the top.

hunks.baseline: After becoming an S-rank Hunter, the world had completely belonged to him.
hunks.sol: Once he became an S-rank Hunter, the world had belonged to him.

hunks.baseline: No matter what major disaster he caused, the worst that happened was being summoned by his father and scolded a few times. He had never cared about the criticism from the public or opposing factions.
hunks.sol: No matter how big a scandal he caused, the worst consequence was being summoned by his father and scolded a few times. He had never cared when the public or opposing factions denounced him.

hunks.baseline: An S-rank Hunter was the face of a nation and another name for national power. No matter how much public opinion pointed fingers at him, that fact did not change. That was reality.
hunks.sol: An S-rank Hunter was the face of a nation, another name for its national power. No matter how harshly public opinion condemned him, that fact remained unchanged.
That was reality.

hunks.baseline: Was that why he had become more passionate about media interviews and parties than smelly, dirty raids? Why he had stopped training and started using drugs?
hunks.sol: Was that why he had become more interested in media interviews and parties than filthy, foul-smelling raids? Why he had stopped training and started doing drugs?

hunks.baseline: But the first war he had ever experienced was chaotic, and watching the monster armies advance endlessly day after day made it difficult to breathe.
hunks.sol: But the first war of his life was chaos. Watching the monster armies surge forward without end, day after day, left him struggling to breathe.

hunks.baseline: For someone who had walked an elite course paved with diamonds, it was an unbearably difficult environment.
hunks.sol: For someone who had followed an elite path paved with diamonds, it was an unbearably harsh environment.

hunks.baseline: On top of that, there was one person whose influence still lingered behind Wu Heixing’s repeated mistakes.
hunks.sol: On top of that, one person’s influence lingered behind Wu Heixing’s repeated mistakes.

hunks.baseline: A wall even greater than Lei Fei, the object of his long-standing jealousy—the second such wall he had encountered in his life.
hunks.sol: The second wall he had encountered in his life—and one far greater than Lei Fei, the object of his long-standing jealousy.

hunks.baseline: The shadow Jin Taekyung cast was broad and dark.
hunks.sol: The shadow Jin Taekyung cast was vast and dark.

hunks.baseline: The fear carved deep into Wu Heixing’s mind by his one-sided defeat would never be shaken off as long as Jin Taekyung remained.
hunks.sol: The fear carved deep into Wu Heixing’s mind by that one-sided defeat would never leave him as long as Jin Taekyung remained.

hunks.baseline: An inexplicable light flashed in Wu Heixing’s eyes as he stared at the ceiling.
hunks.sol: An inscrutable light flashed in Wu Heixing’s eyes as he stared at the ceiling.

hunks.baseline: Recalling the conversation he had shared with Lee Jungryong on the night of his terrible defeat, he smiled. The anger that had been boiling hot had disappeared long ago.
hunks.sol: He smiled, recalling the conversation he had shared with Lee Jungryong on the night of his crushing defeat. His boiling anger had already vanished without a trace.

hunks.sol: Once he calmed down, the exhaustion he had forgotten came rushing back, weighing heavily on his eyelids. As sleep overtook him, Wu Heixing had one last thought.

hunks.sol: *Damn it. How many more battles like today’s are we going to have to fight?*
